 BASKETBALL Los Angeles Lakers LA Lakers vs Phoenix Suns: Where to watch today's game and What time is the face off at Footprint Centre
 Western Conference-leading Lakers visit Suns looking to get back on track at Footprint Centre
 LA Lakers vs Phoenix Suns Special 
 BEATRIZ RODRÍGUEZ
 Updated 15/11/2026
 -
 10:59 CST 
 Follow MARCA on Google

 This Sunday, November 15, 2026, the Footprint Centre in Phoenix hosts one of those matchups the NBA loves to sell: the Phoenix Suns, still trying to find their best form, against the Los Angeles Lakers, who arrive as the best team in the entire league.
 It's the clash between a streaking Western giant and a home team desperately needing points to climb out of the bottom of the Western Conference.
 Lip reader reveals what Detroit fan allegedly told Austin Reaves during heated Lakers game The outlook for Lakers vs. Suns before tip-off
 The picture in the standings says it all. The Lakers lead both the Western Conference and the overall NBA standings with a record of 11 wins and 2 losses (.846), the best winning percentage in the league. Their offense is a machine: they have scored 1,588 points, the highest total in the entire competition, with a +103 differential.
 Across the way, the Suns are navigating troubled waters. With a 4-6 (.400) record, they sit in third place in the Pacific Division and 19th overall, 5.5 games behind tonight’s opponent. Their point differential is negative (-53), a reflection of a season start that has alternated flashes of promise with hard setbacks.
 Two streaks heading in opposite directions
 The Lakers come in on a roll. In their most recent outings, they put together a remarkable winning streak: 131-125 against Toronto, a commanding 138-117 over Miami, 116-103 in Sacramento, 121-116 in Detroit, 124-114 in Atlanta and, most recently, a 123-112 road win over Milwaukee. 
 The only recent blemish was a 129-136 loss to Portland. It's a team that wins both at home and on the road, and that makes it a feared visitor.
 Phoenix, on the other hand, has been inconsistent. It is coming off a solid 133-110 win over the Clippers, but before that it had suffered a crushing 96-122 loss to San Antonio on its own court. In the previous stretch it had also accumulated setbacks against Golden State (113-116) and Portland (119-132), interspersed with close wins such as the 102-99 victory over Houston.
 The good news for the fans: when the Suns play at Footprint Centre with their best energy, they are capable of beating anyone, as they showed by defeating the Warriors 131-122.
 LA Lakers vs Phoenix Suns: Where to watch it live and what time it starts
 The game between the Phoenix Suns and the Los Angeles Lakers will be played on Sunday, November 15, 2026 at 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time (3:00 p.m. Central Time and 1:00 p.m. Pacific Time ) at Phoenix's Footprint Centre, which has a capacity of 18,422 fans.
 In the United States, the local broadcast will be available on Arizona"s Family 3TV and the Suns Live service in the Phoenix market, while in the Los Angeles market it can be watched on Spectrum Sports Net and its streaming platform Spectrum Sports Net +.
 The showdown under the microscope: Los Angeles' artillery against Phoenix's
 The biggest appeal is in the backcourts. For the Lakers, Slovenian Luka Dončić is the absolute engine of that league-leading offense, supported by Austin Reaves and Collin Sexton in a deep rotation that also features shooters like Quentin Grimes and defensive specialists like Matisse Thybulle. In the paint, Walker Kessler and veteran Kevon Looney provide presence and rebounding.
 The Suns are clinging to their franchise cornerstone Devin Booker, joined by the explosive Jalen Green on the perimeter and the interior duo of Dillon Brooks and Miles Bridges to carry the offensive load.
 At the center, Mark Williams and young South Sudanese Khaman Maluach will have the difficult task of containing the opponent's playmaking. For Phoenix, limiting the pace and transition will be key: when the game opens up, the Los Angeles offense punishes without mercy.
 What’s at stake in the NBA standings
 For the Lakers, the objective is clear: maintain the top spot in the West and in the league. With San Antonio (10-2) and Houston (9-3) right on their heels in the conference, every win matters to preserve the lead and home-court advantage heading into the postseason. A victory in Phoenix would reaffirm their status as favorites. 
 For the Suns, the game is purely about survival in the standings. 5.5 games behind the tenth spot that marks the play-in zone in the West — currently held by Denver (6-4) — Phoenix cannot afford to lose ground against direct rivals.
 Beating a leader like the Lakers would be, in addition to three emotional boosts, a statement of intent that the season still has a long way to go.
 The Suns are not yet in an irreversible crisis, but their 19th-place overall standing and losing record place them closer to the bottom of the West than to the play-in spots. 
 Below them in the Pacific are the Clippers (2-8) and the free-falling Kings (1-10), so the immediate benchmark for Phoenix is to avoid losing touch with the group of chasers. A string of defeats against rivals from their conference could bury them in the trailing pack before November is over.
 What is the prediction for Lakers vs Suns?
 The numbers and the moment clearly favor Los Angeles: league leaders, a devastating offense, and a winning streak at home and on the road. That said, the home-court factor and the firepower of Booker and Green give Phoenix a path to pull off an upset if they can slow the pace.
 The reasonable bet is a high-scoring game with the Lakers prevailing, although the Suns have what it takes to make it uncomfortable.
